_why: D3 and D4 of the grok-codex-fallback gap report. D3: the grok child's CLAUDE* scrub enumerated names with `compgen -e`, which lists only shell identifiers, so `CLAUDE-HYPHEN=`/`CLAUDE.DOT=` reached the child against FR-3's `^CLAUDE` class. D4: the exec heartbeat appended `#hmad-beat` into the transcript between the two write()s of one event, splitting a grok `end` and turning a completed run into TRUNCATED.
_provenance: docs/archive/2026-09/grok-codex-fallback/grok-codex-fallback.gap.v1.md, sections D3 and D4; both reproduced at 182a1e34 before the fix.

mutations.name: scrub-enumerates-compgen
mutations._mechanism: Enumerate names from `compgen -e` again. Non-identifier CLAUDE names are invisible to it and reach the grok child. HOST-BOUND, measured 2026-10-04: on a host whose ambient bash is macOS /bin/bash 3.2, `compgen -e` DOES list `CLAUDE-HYPHEN`/`KEEP-HYPHEN` (probe: `env 'CLAUDE-HYPHEN=x' /bin/bash -c 'compgen -e'`), so this mutant is equivalent there and reports SURVIVED. It discriminates only under bash 4+, where D3 was found.

mutations.name: scrub-drops-unset
mutations._mechanism: Match CLAUDE* names but never add `-u`. Every CLAUDE name reaches the child.
mutations.find:
case "$_v" in CLAUDE*) child_env+=(-u "$_v") ;; esac
  done

mutations.name: beat-ignores-line-boundary
mutations._mechanism: Beat whenever a beat log is set, regardless of the log's last byte. The beat lands inside a split event again.

mutations.name: beat-never-written
mutations._mechanism: Make the boundary gate always false. No beat reaches the transcript, so a silent-but-alive run and a dead one look alike.
